-- Migration: add_checklist_and_housekeeping_task_columns
-- Description: Adds property-scoped checklist table; extends housekeeping_tasks with
--              reservation link, priority, and scheduled window (timestamps).
-- Created: 2026-04-20

-- ============================================================================
-- Checklist (property-scoped templates / definitions)
-- ============================================================================

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.checklist (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    property_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES public.properties(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    description TEXT,
    item JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
    created_by UUID NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_checklist_property_id
    ON public.checklist (property_id);

COMMENT ON TABLE public.checklist IS
    'Property-scoped checklist definitions with structured items stored as JSON.';

-- ============================================================================
-- Housekeeping tasks: reservation, priority, schedule window
-- ============================================================================

ALTER TABLE public.housekeeping_tasks
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS reservation_id UUID REFERENCES public.reservations(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS priority VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium'
        CHECK (priority IN ('low', 'medium', 'high', 'urgent')),
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS start_date TIMESTAMPTZ,
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS end_date TIMESTAMPTZ;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_housekeeping_tasks_reservation_id
    ON public.housekeeping_tasks (reservation_id);

COMMENT ON COLUMN public.housekeeping_tasks.reservation_id IS
    'Optional link to the reservation this task is associated with.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.housekeeping_tasks.priority IS
    'Relative urgency: low, medium, high, urgent.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.housekeeping_tasks.start_date IS
    'Scheduled start (date and time in UTC).';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.housekeeping_tasks.end_date IS
    'Scheduled end (date and time in UTC).';

-- ============================================================================
-- Row Level Security (checklist)
-- ============================================================================

ALTER TABLE public.checklist ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Service role full access on checklist"

## Checklist Integration into Housekeeping Tasks — Deep Scout Report

### 1. Checklist Template Attachment on Task Creation (`add-task-dialog.tsx`)

**Flow:**

```
User selects checklist template from dropdown
  ↓
onValueChange fires with selected template UUID
  ↓
Client calls HousekeepingQueries.getChecklistTemplateItem(uuid) directly via Supabase
  ↓
Response: JSONB from checklist.item column
  ↓
parseChecklistTemplateLines() normalizes to Array<{ id, label, notes }>
  ↓
Missing IDs get fallback: `${templateId}-${index + 1}`
  ↓
State populated:
  - checklistItems[]: display list (id, label, notes)
  - form.checklistItemDone[]: all initialized to { item_id, status: "pending" }
  ↓
Checklist items rendered as read-only bordered cards (no checkboxes in Add)
  ↓
On submit: both checklistTemplateId AND checklistItemDone sent to API
```

**Key behavior:**
- The template selector is a `<Select>` with a "None" default option.
- When switching away from "None", the dialog fetches template items client-side (not through the REST API) using `createClient()` → `HousekeepingQueries`.
- All items start as `"pending"` — no completion state on creation.
- If no template is selected, `checklistItemDone` defaults to `form.checklistItemDone ?? []` (empty).

**Form state shape** (`AddHousekeepingTaskInput`):
```ts
checklistTemplateId?: string | null   // UUID of selected template, or null
checklistItemDone?: Array<{ item_id: string; status: "pending" | "completed" }>
```

### 2. Checklist Template Attachment on Task Edit (`edit-task-dialog.tsx`)

**Flow on dialog open:**

```
Dialog opens with existing task data
  ↓
form populated from task.checklistId and task.checklistItemDone
  ↓
useEffect detects form.checklistTemplateId
  ↓
Fetches template items via getChecklistTemplateItem(checklistId)
  ↓
Merges template items with EXISTING completion state:
  - Creates Set of completed item_ids from task.checklistItemDone
  - Each item gets checked: selectedDone.has(id)
  ↓
checklistItems[] = Array<{ id, label, notes, checked: boolean }>
```

**Key behavior:**
- Items render with **interactive checkboxes** (unlike Add which is read-only display).
- Each `<Checkbox>` toggles `item.checked` in local state.
- **Changing the template clears items**: When `onValueChange` fires with a new template or "none", `checklistItemDone` resets to `[]` and `checklistItems` clears. The `useEffect` then re-fetches for the new template.
- **Items without existing completion data default to unchecked** (the Set is empty for new item_ids).
- On submit, `checklistItemDone` is rebuilt from local state:
  ```ts
  checklistItems.map(item => ({
    item_id: item.id,
    status: item.checked ? "completed" : "pending"
  }))
  ```

### 3. Checklist Display in Task Details (`task-details-dialog.tsx`)

**Flow:**

```
Dialog opens
  ↓
useEffect: if task.checklistId exists
  ↓
Creates Set of completed IDs from task.checklistItemDone
  ↓
Fetches full template via getChecklistTemplateById(checklistId)
  ↓
parseChecklistTemplateLines() normalizes template.item JSONB
  ↓
Displays:
  - Checklist name (template.name)
  - Each item with "Completed" or "Pending" label
  ↓
NO interactive toggling — read-only display
```

**UI structure:**
```
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│ Task details                │
│ "Task title"                │
│─────────────────────────────│
│ Site        │ Site Name     │
│ Description │ Desc text     │
│ Assignee    │ Staff name    │
│ Status      │ [Pending]     │
│ Checklist   │               │
│   Template Name             │
│   ┌─────────────────────┐   │
│   │ Item 1    Completed │   │
│   └─────────────────────┘   │
│   ┌─────────────────────┐   │
│   │ Item 2    Pending   │   │
│   └─────────────────────┘   │
│─────────────────────────────│

└─────────────────────────────┘
```

**Important:** The table row (`housekeeping-table.tsx`) does **NOT** display checklist progress inline. There is no column for checklist completion % or item count in the task list table. The checklist is only visible by opening "View task" or "Edit task" dialogs.

### 4. Checklist Columns in API Route Handlers

**POST `/api/v1/properties/[propertyId]/housekeeping`** (create task):


**PATCH `/api/v1/properties/[propertyId]/housekeeping/[housekeepingId]`** (update task):

```ts

await queries.updateHousekeepingTask({
  id: housekeepingId,
  propertyId,
  checklistId: parsed.data.checklistTemplateId,      // → checklist_id column
  checklistItemDone: parsed.data.checklistItemDone,   // → checklist_item_done column (as JSON)
})
// Plus: auto-site-availability logic (see §5 below)
```

**In `housekeeping-queries.ts`:**

```ts
// createHousekeepingTask:
insertRow = {
  ...
  checklist_id: input.checklistId ?? null,
  checklist_item_done: input.checklistItemDone as unknown as Json,
}

// updateHousekeepingTask:
updateRow = {
  ...
  checklist_id: input.checklistId,        // only if !== undefined
  checklist_item_done: input.checklistItemDone as unknown as Json,  // only if !== undefined
}
```

Both `checklist_id` and `checklist_item_done` are **optional** on update — they're only included when present in the input. This means you can update just the completion state without changing the template, or change the template without updating item states (though the latter would leave stale item_ids).

```
  ↓
```

**What does NOT happen:**
- ❌ No check that all checklist items are marked "completed"
- ❌ No check that a checklist even exists
- ❌ No checklist progress percentage displayed in the confirmation dialog
- ❌ No warning if items are still pending
- ❌ The `checklistItemDone` array is not touched at all during completion

**Result:** A task can be marked "done" with 0% checklist completion. The checklist tracking is purely informational and has no enforcement on the task lifecycle.

### 6. Zod Validation Schemas — Checklist Fields

**`ChecklistItemDoneRequestSchema`** (used by both Create and Update task):
```ts
z.object({
  item_id: z.string().trim().min(1).max(120),        // any string, not UUID-validated
  status: z.enum(['pending', 'completed']),
})
```

**`CreateHousekeepingTaskRequestSchema`** — checklist-related fields:
```ts
checklistTemplateId: z.preprocess(
  emptyStringToUndefined,
  z.string().uuid().optional()          // must be valid UUID if provided
),
checklistItemDone: z.array(
  ChecklistItemDoneRequestSchema
).optional(),                           // 0..N items, or omitted entirely
```

**`UpdateHousekeepingTaskRequestSchema`** — checklist-related fields:
```ts
checklistTemplateId: z.preprocess(
  emptyStringToUndefined,
  z.string().uuid().optional()
),
checklistItemDone: z.array(
  ChecklistItemDoneRequestSchema
).optional(),
// Plus top-level refine: Object.keys(payload).length > 0
```

**Notable validation gaps:**
- `item_id` is `z.string()` (not UUID) — accepts any non-empty string up to 120 chars. This matches the fallback ID scheme (`${templateId}-${index}`) used client-side.
- No cross-field validation between `checklistTemplateId` and `checklistItemDone` — you can send items for a template that doesn't match, or items without a template.
- No uniqueness constraint on `item_id` within the array.
- No minimum length on `checklistItemDone` array (can send empty array).

### Complete Integration Flow Summary

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    CHECKLIST TEMPLATE MANAGEMENT                 │
│  (Separate "Checklist" tab in housekeeping page)                 │
│                                                                  │
│  Create template: name + description + items[{id,label,notes}]  │
│  → Stored in `checklist` table, `item` column as JSONB          │
│  → Templates are property-scoped (property_id FK)               │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │
                           │ Template selected by UUID
                           ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    TASK CREATION (Add)                           │
│                                                                  │
│  1. User selects template → client fetches template items       │
│  2. All items init to status:"pending"                          │
│  3. Items shown read-only (no checkboxes)                       │
│  4. Submit sends: checklistTemplateId + checklistItemDone       │
│  5. API validates template belongs to property                  │
│  6. Writes to housekeeping_tasks:                               │
│     checklist_id = template UUID                                │
│     checklist_item_done = [{item_id, status}] JSON              │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │
                           ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    TASK EDITING                                   │
│                                                                  │
│  1. Existing task loads with checklistId + checklistItemDone    │
│  2. Client fetches template items, merges with saved state      │
│  3. Items shown WITH interactive checkboxes                     │
│  4. User toggles completion per item                            │
│  5. Submit sends updated checklistItemDone (full replacement)   │
│  6. Can also swap templates (clears completion state)           │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │
                           ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    TASK VIEWING (Read-only)                       │
│                                                                  │
│  1. Fetches template by checklistId                             │
│  2. Merges template items with saved completion state           │
│  3. Displays "Completed" / "Pending" text labels                │
│  4. No toggling possible                                       │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │
                           ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    TASK COMPLETION                                │
│                                                                  │
│  1. User clicks "Complete task" from row dropdown               │
│  2. AlertDialog confirmation (no checklist info shown)           │
│  3. PATCH { status: "done" } — no checklist data sent           │
│  4. ❌ NO validation of checklist completion                    │
│  5. Side effect: if last open task for site → site=available    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Key Risks & Observations

| # | Finding | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **No checklist enforcement on completion** — task can be marked done with 0% items checked | Medium (data integrity) |
| 2 | **Stale item_ids on template swap** — editing a task and changing the template sends the old template's item completion states; no reconciliation occurs | Low (UI resets items, but saved state could diverge) |
| 3 | **`item_id` not UUID-validated** in Zod — accepts arbitrary strings, which is intentional for fallback IDs but makes Referential integrity to template impossible | Low (by design) |
| 4 | **Checklist panel fetches client-side** (bypasses API/RBAC) — inconsistent with task data flow through REST API | Low (inconsistency) |
| 5 | **No checklist progress in task table** — users must open task details to see completion status; no column or badge | Medium (UX gap) |
| 6 | **Completion dialog doesn't show checklist status** — user has no visibility into item progress when confirming completion | Medium (UX) |

## Post-Checkout Housekeeping Task Creation — Deep Scout Report

### 1. Entry Points That Trigger Checkout

There are **two distinct entry points** that open the `CheckOutDialog`:

| Entry Point | File | Trigger Context |
|---|---|---|
| **Dashboard "Today's Departures"** | `src/components/dashboard/reservations/departure-check-out-button.tsx` | Standalone button on property dashboard showing today's checked-in guests |
| **Reservation Actions Dropdown** | `src/components/admin/check-out-button.tsx` → `src/components/admin/reservation-actions.tsx` | "⋯" dropdown menu on reservation detail dialog, reservations table, and timeline |

Both follow the same pattern:
1. User clicks "Check Out" button/menu item
2. Fetches full reservation data via `GET /api/v1/reservations/{id}`
3. Opens `CheckOutDialog` with the fetched `reservation` object (including nested `guest` and `site` data)

### 2. The Complete Checkout → Housekeeping Task Flow

The entire flow lives inside **`src/components/dashboard/reservations/check-out-dialog.tsx`**. It's a **three-stage sequential dialog chain**:

```
Stage 1: CheckOutDialog (main checkout form)
  ↓ User fills out + clicks "Complete Check-out"
Stage 2: Follow-up AlertDialog (post-checkout prompt)
  ↓ User chooses "Create Housekeeping Task"
Stage 3: AddTaskDialog (reused housekeeping task form)
  ↓ User submits → POST API call
Done: Task created, dialogs close, page refreshes
```

**State machine in `CheckOutDialog`:**
```
isProcessing          → during checkout API call
showLateCheckOutWarning → AlertDialog if checking out after configured time
showFollowUpTaskDialog → post-checkout prompt dialog
isCreateTaskDialogOpen → AddTaskDialog open state
isCreatingTask        → during housekeeping task API call
```

### 3. Stage 1: Checkout Execution

The checkout dialog displays:
- **Guest Information**: name, email, confirmation #, status badge
- **Stay Summary**: site (with current status badge), check-in/check-out dates, nights, guest count, total amount
- **Outstanding Balance Warning**: if `total_amount > paid_amount`
- **Site Inspection**: damages checkbox + mandatory notes if damages reported
- **Check-out Notes**: free text

**Pre-checkout validations (client-side):**
- Late check-out detection: compares current time against property's `checkOutTime` config → shows `showLateCheckOutWarning` AlertDialog
- Check-out day restrictions: compares today's weekday against `allowedCheckOutDays` from booking rules
- If damages checked, notes are required

**Checkout API call:**
```
POST /api/v1/reservations/{reservationId}/check-out
Body: { hasDamages: boolean, notes: string | null }
```

**Server-side (`check-out/route.ts`):**
1. Auth + RBAC check (`reservations.check_out` permission)
2. Validates reservation exists via `CheckOutGuestCommandHandler`
3. Enforces check-out day restrictions from `booking_rules_config`
4. Executes `CheckOutGuestCommandHandler.execute()` which calls `reservation.checkOut()` on the domain model
5. **Auto-sets site status to `'housekeeping'`** via direct Supabase update
6. Records activity logs for both the reservation checkout and site status change

**Critical finding: The API does NOT auto-create a housekeeping task.** Task creation is entirely client-driven after the checkout API returns successfully. The `CheckOutGuestCommand` publishes domain events (`getEventBus().publishAll(...)`) but there are **no event subscribers** that create housekeeping tasks — confirmed by grepping `src/modules/BookingEngine` and `src/shared/infrastructure` for "housekeeping" (zero matches).

### 4. Stage 2: Follow-up Task Prompt

After checkout succeeds:
```ts
onOpenChange(false)          // closes main checkout dialog
setShowFollowUpTaskDialog(true)  // opens follow-up prompt
```

The follow-up dialog is an `AlertDialog` (styled as a dialog) with:
- **Title**: "Create follow-up task"
- **Description**: `"{firstName} {lastName} just checked out of {siteName}. Would you like to create a housekeeping task to prepare the unit?"`
- **Two buttons**: "Skip" and "Create Housekeeping Task"

**User has three paths:**

| Choice | Action |
|---|---|
| Click **"Skip"** | `handleSkipFollowUpTask()` → closes everything, calls `router.refresh()` |
| Click **"Create Housekeeping Task"** | `handleCreateHousekeepingTask()` → closes follow-up, opens `AddTaskDialog` |
| Close via overlay/X | Triggers `onOpenChange(false)` → same as Skip |

### 5. Stage 3: AddTaskDialog with Pre-filled Data

When the user clicks "Create Housekeeping Task", the `AddTaskDialog` opens with these pre-filled values:

```ts
const followUpSiteOptions = reservation.site_id
  ? [{ id: reservation.site_id, label: followUpSiteLabel }]
  : []

const followUpInitialValues = {
  siteId: reservation.site_id,                              // ← pre-filled
  siteName: followUpSiteLabel,                               // ← pre-filled  
  reservationConfirmationId: reservation.confirmation_number, // ← pre-filled
}
```

**What's pre-filled:**
| Field | Source | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `siteId` | `reservation.site_id` | UUID of the reservation's site |
| `siteName` | `reservation.site.site_name ?? site.site_number` | Display label |
| `reservationConfirmationId` | `reservation.confirmation_number` | Links task to reservation |
| `siteOptions` | Single-item array from reservation | User cannot choose a different site |
| `checklistOptions` | Fetched client-side from `checklist` table | All templates for the property |
| `assigneeOptions` | Fetched from `/api/v1/properties/{propertyId}/housekeeping/assignees` | Active housekeeping staff |

**What's NOT pre-filled (user must fill manually):**
- Task title (required)
- Description (optional)
- Assignee (optional — defaults to "Unassigned")
- Priority (defaults to "Medium")
- Status (defaults to "Pending")
- Start date / due date
- Checklist template selection (if any templates exist for the property)

**Special differences from normal task creation:**

| Aspect | Normal (from housekeeping page) | Post-checkout |
|---|---|---|
| `siteOptions` | All non-deleted sites for property | **Single site only** (locked to reservation's site) |
| `reservationConfirmationId` | Manually entered (optional) | **Auto-filled** from reservation |
| Checklist/assignee options | Loaded by server component, passed as props | **Loaded client-side** via Supabase direct + REST API |
| Submit handler | `handleAddTask` in `housekeeping-page-content.tsx` | `handleCreateTaskFromReservation` in `check-out-dialog.tsx` |
| Post-submit action | Toast + reload tasks | Toast + `router.refresh()` + close all dialogs |

### 6. Task Creation API Call (Post-Checkout)

The `handleCreateTaskFromReservation` function in `check-out-dialog.tsx` calls:
```
POST /api/v1/properties/{reservation.property_id}/housekeeping
Body: {
  siteId: input.siteId || reservation.site_id,
  staffId: input.assigneeId ?? null,
  title: input.task,
  description: ...,
  status: toApiStatus(input.status),          // "Pending" → "pending"
  reservationConfirmationId: reservation.confirmation_number,  // ← hardcoded from reservation
  priority: toApiPriority(input.priority),
  startDate: ...,
  dueDate: ...,
  checklistTemplateId: ...,
  checklistItemDone: ...
}
```

This is the **exact same API endpoint** used by the normal housekeeping page (`housekeeping-page-content.tsx` → `handleAddTask`). The only difference is:
1. `reservationConfirmationId` is guaranteed to be the checkout reservation's confirmation number (not manually typed)
2. `siteId` falls back to `reservation.site_id` if the form's value is empty

### 7. How Checklist Options Are Loaded (Post-Checkout Context)

The `CheckOutDialog` loads two datasets client-side via `useEffect`:

**Checklist templates** — direct Supabase client query:
```ts
const supabase = createClient()
const { data } = await supabase
  .from('checklist')
  .select('id, name')
  .eq('property_id', reservation.property_id)
  .order('name', { ascending: true })
```

**Assignee options** — REST API call:
```ts
const response = await fetch(`/api/v1/properties/${reservation.property_id}/housekeeping/assignees`)
// Returns: { data: { assigneeOptions: [{ id, label }] } }
```

Both load when the dialog first renders (dependency: `reservation.property_id`). They're available immediately when the `AddTaskDialog` opens.

### 8. Alternative Flow: URL Parameter Based

There is a **second mechanism** for pre-filling the AddTaskDialog — URL query parameters on the housekeeping page:

In `housekeeping-page-content.tsx`:
```ts
const searchParams = useSearchParams()
const addTaskInitialValues = useMemo(() => {
  const siteId = searchParams.get("siteId") ?? ""
  const reservationConfirmationId = searchParams.get("reservationConfirmationId") ?? ""
  // ...
}, [searchParams, siteOptions])

useEffect(() => {
  if (!canCreateTask) return
  if (searchParams.get("openAddTask") !== "1") return
  setIsAddTaskDialogOpen(true)
  // Cleans up URL params after opening
}, [canCreateTask, searchParams, router, propertyId])
```

Navigating to `/dashboard/{propertyId}/housekeeping?openAddTask=1&siteId={uuid}&reservationConfirmationId={conf}` would auto-open the AddTaskDialog with site and reservation pre-filled. However, **this mechanism does not appear to be actively used by the checkout flow** — the checkout dialog handles everything inline.

## Site Status Update on Housekeeping Task Completion — Deep Scout Report

### 1. Complete-Task-Confirmation-Dialog → API Call

**File:** `src/components/dashboard/housekeeping/housekeeping-dialog.tsx/complete-task-confirmation-dialog.tsx`

The dialog sends exactly one field to the API:

```ts
PATCH /api/v1/properties/{propertyId}/housekeeping/{taskId}
Body: JSON.stringify({ status: "done" })
```

**What it does NOT send:**
- No `checklistItemDone` — completion state is not touched
- No `title`, `description`, `staffId`, etc. — nothing else changes
- No site-related data — site status change is a server-side side effect

The dialog receives only `{ id, task, siteName }` of the task — no checklist info, no site status info. There's no UI indication of whether other tasks are open for the same site, or what the current site status is.

### 2. `HousekeepingQueries.updateHousekeepingTask()`

**File:** `src/lib/dashboard/housekeeping/housekeeping-queries.ts`

```ts
async updateHousekeepingTask(input: UpdateHousekeepingTaskInput): Promise<HousekeepingTaskRow> {
  const updateRow = {
    // Only includes fields that are !== undefined in the input
    ...(input.status !== undefined ? { status: input.status } : {}),
    // ... other optional fields
  }

  const { data, error } = await this.supabase
    .from('housekeeping_tasks')
    .update(updateRow)
    .eq('id', input.id)          // scopes to specific task
    .eq('property_id', input.propertyId)  // scopes to property (RLS defense-in-depth)
    .select()
    .single()

  if (error) throw ...
  if (!data) throw ...
  return data
}
```

**Key behaviors:**
- Uses the **authenticated client** Supabase instance (subject to RLS)
- Scopes by both `id` and `property_id`
- Returns the full updated row — the caller reads `data.status` from the return value to decide whether to proceed with site logic
- Does NOT set `updated_at` manually — that's handled by a DB trigger (`trigger_update_housekeeping_tasks_updated_at`)

### 3. Site Availability Logic in the PATCH Handler

**File:** `src/app/api/v1/properties/[propertyId]/housekeeping/[housekeepingId]/route.ts`

The site status change is a **post-update side effect** in the PATCH handler. After `updateHousekeepingTask()` returns successfully:

```
Step 1: Check if the task's status is now 'done'
  ↓ (only if yes)
Step 2: Count remaining open tasks for the same site
  ↓
Step 3: If openForSite === 0
  ↓
Step 4: Load site row via service-role client
  ↓
Step 5: Check if site status is 'housekeeping' or 'maintenance'
  ↓ (only if yes)
Step 6: Update site status to 'available'
  ↓
Step 7: Log activity
```

**Precise condition chain:**

```ts
// Gate 1: Task must be done
if (housekeepingTask.status === 'done') {

  // Gate 2: No other open tasks for this site
  const openForSite = await queries.countOpenHousekeepingTasksForSite(
    propertyId, housekeepingTask.site_id
  )

  if (openForSite === 0) {

    // Gate 3: Load site via SERVICE ROLE (bypasses RLS)
    const service = createServiceRoleClient()
    const { data: siteRow } = await service
      .from('sites')
      .select('id, status, site_name, site_number')
      .eq('id', housekeepingTask.site_id)
      .eq('property_id', propertyId)
      .is('deleted_at', null)
      .maybeSingle()

    // Gate 4: Site status must be 'housekeeping' or 'maintenance'
    const normalizedStatus = (siteRow.status ?? '').trim().toLowerCase()
    if (normalizedStatus === 'housekeeping' || normalizedStatus === 'maintenance') {

      // UPDATE: Set site to available
      await service
        .from('sites')
        .update({ status: 'available', updated_at: timestamp })
        .eq('id', siteRow.id)
        .eq('property_id', propertyId)
        .is('deleted_at', null)

      // Audit log
      await recordActivityLog(service, {
        action: 'update',
        resource: 'site',
        userId: null,    // ← system action, no user attribution
        details: `Site ${siteLabel} marked available after last housekeeping task was completed.`
      })
    }
  }
}
```

**All four conditions must be true for the site to transition to `available`:**

| Gate | Condition | If false |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `housekeepingTask.status === 'done'` | Skip entire block (no site check) |
| 2 | `openForSite === 0` | Skip — logs "other open tasks for this site" |
| 3 | `siteRow` exists and not deleted | Skip — logs warning |
| 4 | `normalizedStatus === 'housekeeping' \|\| 'maintenance'` | Skip — logs "site status is not housekeeping or maintenance" |

### 4. `countOpenHousekeepingTasksForSite()`

```ts
async countOpenHousekeepingTasksForSite(propertyId: string, siteId: string): Promise<number> {
  const { count, error } = await this.supabase
    .from('housekeeping_tasks')
    .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
    .eq('property_id', propertyId)
    .eq('site_id', siteId)
    .neq('status', 'done')           // ← counts everything NOT 'done'

  return count ?? 0
}
```

**Query translates to:**
```sql
SELECT COUNT(id) FROM housekeeping_tasks
WHERE property_id = $1
  AND site_id = $2
  AND status != 'done'
```

**What counts as "open":** `pending` and `in_progress` — anything that is not `done`.

### 5. Site Status Values — The Mismatch

There are **three different definitions** of valid site statuses across the codebase:

**A) Database CHECK constraint** (`supabase/migrations/20250203100000_add_reserved_booked_site_statuses.sql`):
```sql
CHECK (status IN (
  'available', 'reserved', 'booked', 'occupied',
  'housekeeping', 'maintenance', 'unavailable'
))
```
→ 7 values including `'housekeeping'` and `'unavailable'`

**B) Domain model enum** (`src/modules/SiteManagement/domain/SiteStatus.ts`):
```ts

  AVAILABLE = 'available',
  OCCUPIED = 'occupied',
  RESERVED = 'reserved',
  NEEDS_HOUSEKEEPING = 'needs_housekeeping',   // ← different from DB
  OUT_OF_SERVICE = 'out_of_service',             // ← different from DB
  BOOKED = 'booked',
  // NOTE: no 'maintenance', no 'unavailable'
}
```
→ 6 values, **no `'maintenance'`**, **no `'unavailable'`**, uses `'needs_housekeeping'` instead of `'housekeeping'`

**C) Booking types** (`src/lib/booking/types.ts`):
```ts

  | 'available' | 'reserved' | 'booked' | 'occupied'
  | 'housekeeping' | 'maintenance' | 'unavailable'
```
→ 7 values, matches DB constraint

**D) API Zod schema** (`src/types/api/v1/schemas/sites.ts`):
```ts

  'available', 'occupied', 'reserved',
  'needs_housekeeping',  // ← different from DB
  'out_of_service',      // ← different from DB
  'booked',

```
→ 6 values, matches domain model, **doesn't match DB constraint**

### 6. 🔴 Critical Bug: Status Value Mismatch

The checkout route writes `'housekeeping'` to the database:
```ts
// check-out/route.ts line 168
.update({ status: 'housekeeping' })
```

The housekeeping PATCH handler checks for `'housekeeping'` and `'maintenance'`:
```ts
// [housekeepingId]/route.ts
if (normalizedStatus === 'housekeeping' || normalizedStatus === 'maintenance')
```

The DB CHECK constraint allows `'housekeeping'`. **This path works correctly.**

However, the **domain model** and **sites API schema** use `'needs_housekeeping'` (not `'housekeeping'`). This means:

| Layer | Value Written | Value Checked | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Checkout API → DB | `'housekeeping'` ✅ | — | DB accepts it (CHECK constraint allows it) |
| Housekeeping PATCH → DB read | — | `'housekeeping'` ✅ | Matches, site transitions to available |
| Domain model `SiteStatus` | — | `'needs_housekeeping'` | Would NOT match `'housekeeping'` |
| Sites API Zod schema | — | `'needs_housekeeping'` | Would REJECT `'housekeeping'` |

**The housekeeping PATCH handler bypasses the domain model entirely** — it writes directly to the DB via service-role client. The domain model's `isValidStatusTransition()` and `completeHousekeeping()` are never invoked in this flow. This means:
- The site status transition from `housekeeping` → `available` does **not** go through domain validation
- No `SiteStatusChangedEvent` is published for this transition
- The domain model considers `'housekeeping'` an invalid status entirely (it uses `'needs_housekeeping'`)

### 7. Domain Model's Valid Transitions (Unused by HK PATCH)

From `SiteStatus.ts`:
```
AVAILABLE      → [OCCUPIED, RESERVED, OUT_OF_SERVICE, BOOKED]
OCCUPIED       → [NEEDS_HOUSEKEEPING, AVAILABLE]
RESERVED       → [OCCUPIED, AVAILABLE]
NEEDS_HOUSEKEEPING → [AVAILABLE, OUT_OF_SERVICE]
OUT_OF_SERVICE → [AVAILABLE, NEEDS_HOUSEKEEPING]
BOOKED         → [OCCUPIED, AVAILABLE]
```

Note: `NEEDS_HOUSEKEEPING → AVAILABLE` is the domain's equivalent of the PATCH handler's `'housekeeping' → 'available'` logic. But the PATCH handler doesn't use the domain.

### Edge Cases

| Scenario | What Happens |
|---|---|
| **Multiple open tasks for the same site** | `openForSite > 0` → site stays unchanged. Completing one task when others remain does nothing to site status. |
| **Last open task completed** | `openForSite === 0` → if site is `housekeeping` or `maintenance`, transitions to `available`. |
| **Site already `available` when task completed** | Gate 4 fails (`'available'` ≠ `'housekeeping'`/`'maintenance'`) → skip, no change. |
| **Site is `occupied` when task completed** | Gate 4 fails → skip. Unusual but protected against. |
| **Site is `reserved` or `booked` when task completed** | Gate 4 fails → skip. |
| **Site is `unavailable`** | Gate 4 fails → skip. |
| **Site deleted** (`deleted_at IS NOT NULL`) | Gate 3 fails (`is('deleted_at', null)` returns no row) → skip with warning log. |
| **Task belongs to a different property** | Scoping by `property_id` in both the update and site lookup prevents cross-property manipulation. |
| **Task site_id references a site in another property** | The site lookup also scopes by `propertyId`, so it would find nothing → Gate 3 fails → skip. |
| **Concurrent completions** (race condition) | Two tasks for the same site are completed nearly simultaneously. Both pass Gate 1. The first one to reach the count check sees `openForSite === 1` (the other isn't `done` yet), skips. The second one sees `openForSite === 0`, proceeds. This is **safe** — no double-transition. However, the first completer's count check returns 1 and skips, but their task IS done. If they were the last, the second completer handles the transition. If neither is last, both skip correctly. |
| **RLS blocks the site update** | Impossible — uses service-role client which bypasses RLS. This is intentional because "completing staff may lack sites UPDATE under RLS" (comment in code). |

RBAC Architecture Overview The housekeeping feature uses a **three-layer access control** system: ``` Layer 1: NAV VISIBILITY (can they see the page at all?) → resolveDashboardNavVisibility() / canAccessHousekeepingModule() Layer 2: TASK FILTERING (what tasks appear in the list?) → GET API route: requirePropertyAccess() + staff_id scoping Layer 3: ACTION PERMISSIONS (what CRUD operations are allowed?) → resolveModuleActionAccess() + fallbackForCategory() ``` ### 2. Layer 1: Navigation Visibility **File:** `src/lib/rbac/dashboard-guards.ts` ```ts export function canAccessHousekeepingModule(access: ResolvedAccess): boolean { if (!access.role) return false if (isManagerOrAbove(access.role)) return true // owner/admin/manager: always return staffHasPermission(access.categories, 'housekeeping.view_assigned') // staff: needs category } ``` **Who sees the "Housekeeping" nav link:** | Role | Condition | Result | |---|---|---| | **Owner** | `isManagerOrAbove('owner')` → `true` | ✅ Always visible | | **Admin** | `isManagerOrAbove('admin')` → `true` | ✅ Always visible | | **Manager** | `isManagerOrAbove('manager')` → `true` | ✅ Always visible | | **Staff** | Must have `housekeeping` role category | ✅ Only if assigned to "housekeeping" staff category | | **Staff (no category)** | `staffHasPermission([], ...)` → `false` | ❌ Hidden (backward compat: no categories = 'all' category, which grants `housekeeping.view_assigned`) | **Enforced on page load** (`page.tsx`): ```ts const navVisibility = await resolveDashboardNavVisibility(supabase, propertyId, user.id) if (!navVisibility.housekeepingNavVisible) { redirect(`/dashboard/${propertyId}/access-denied`) } ``` ### 3. Layer 2: Task Filtering (Server-Side) **File:** `src/app/api/v1/properties/[propertyId]/housekeeping/route.ts` — `GET` handler This is the critical filtering logic. The decision tree: ``` Step 1: requirePropertyAccess(permission: 'housekeeping.view_assigned') ↓ (denies access entirely if no property membership) Step 2: Determine if user is "elevated" or "staff" access.isElevated = true → owner/admin/manager access.isElevated = false → staff Step 3a: If ELEVATED (owner/admin/manager): - propertyStaffId = null - Client-provided assigneeId filter is HONORED - Can see ALL tasks for the property (no staff_id scoping) Step 3b: If NOT ELEVATED (staff): - Look up property_staff row for (propertyId, userId) - status must be 'active' or 'pending' - If no staff row found → ERROR: "No active staff assignment" - propertyStaffId = staffRow.id (the property_staff.id, NOT the auth user.id) - Client-provided assigneeId filter is IGNORED - Hard-override: listFilters.assigneeId = propertyStaffId → STAFF CAN ONLY SEE TASKS ASSIGNED TO THEMSELVES ``` **Exact code:** ```ts let propertyStaffId: string | null = null if (!access.isElevated) { const { data: staffRow } = await supabase .from('property_staff') .select('id') .eq('property_id', propertyId) .eq('user_id', user.id) .in('status', ['active', 'pending']) .maybeSingle() if (!staffRow?.id) { return error(...) // "No active staff assignment found for this property." } propertyStaffId = staffRow.id as string } // ... if (access.isElevated) { if (data.assigneeId !== undefined) { listFilters.assigneeId = data.assigneeId // use client value } // else: no assignee filter → see ALL tasks } else if (propertyStaffId) { listFilters.assigneeId = propertyStaffId // FORCE to own staff row } ``` **Open task count is also scoped:** ```ts const openTaskCount = await queries.countOpenHousekeepingTasks( propertyId, propertyStaffId ? { assigneeId: propertyStaffId } : undefined, ) ``` Staff sees their own open task count; elevated users see the property-wide total. ### 4. Layer 3: Action Permissions **File:** `src/lib/dashboard/module-action-access.ts` — `resolveModuleActionAccess()` Resolution order: ``` 1. Is user the property OWNER? → YES: return all actions = true (view, create, update, delete) 2. Look up property_staff assignment for (propertyId, userId) - If no assignment AND isElevated: return all true 3. Resolve staff role from assignment: - role = 'owner' → return all true - role = 'admin' (no categories) → return all true - role = 'admin' with categories → check per-category - role = 'staff' → check per-category - No categories at all (admin) → all true - No categories at all (staff) → all false 4. For each staff category the user belongs to: a. Get category.access.moduleAccessControl.housekeeping b. For each requested action: - If moduleAccessControl has explicit toggle → use it - Else → use fallbackForCategory(role, categoryName) ``` **Fallback function** (`housekeepingFallbackForCategory`): ```ts function housekeepingFallbackForCategory(role, categoryName) { if (role === "owner" || "admin") return { view: true, create: true, update: true, delete: true } if (role === "manager" && category === "housekeeping") return { view: true, create: true, update: true, delete: true } if (role === "staff" && category === "housekeeping") return { view: true, create: false, update: false, delete: false } return { view: false, create: false, update: false, delete: false } } ``` **Permission matrix by role:** | Action | Owner | Admin | Manager (HK category) | Staff (HK category) | Staff (no category) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **View** (page access) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | | **View** (task list) | ✅ All tasks | ✅ All tasks | ✅ All tasks | ✅ Own tasks only | ❌ No access | | **Create** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | | **Update** (edit) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | | **Delete** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | | **Reassign** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | | **Complete** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ### 5. summary:
## Goal
Explore and document the housekeeping checklist feature in the Camp-OS project end-to-end, including: checklist template CRUD, integration into housekeeping tasks, post-checkout task creation flow, and site status auto-transition logic when tasks are completed.

## Constraints & Preferences
- User wants detailed file paths and code-level analysis
- User wants understanding of full integration flows, not just surface-level
- No specific tech constraints mentioned beyond "explore and summarize"

## Progress
### Done
- [x] Mapped all housekeeping/checklist files across the codebase
- [x] Documented checklist template CRUD (API routes + UI dialogs)
- [x] Documented checklist integration into task creation/editing/viewing
- [x] Documented Zod validation schemas for checklist-related fields
- [x] Documented post-checkout → housekeeping task creation flow (3-stage dialog chain)
- [x] Documented site status auto-transition logic on task completion (4-gate condition chain)
- [x] Identified critical bugs: `'housekeeping'` vs `'needs_housekeeping'` status mismatch between DB/checkout API and domain model; no domain events published for site transitions

### In Progress
- [ ] (none — all exploration tasks completed)

### Blocked
- [Issues preventing progress, if any]

## Key Decisions
- **Checkout does NOT auto-create housekeeping tasks**: Entirely user-driven via follow-up prompt dialog after checkout API succeeds
- **Site status set to `'housekeeping'` on checkout**: Written directly to DB bypassing domain model, which uses `'needs_housekeeping'`
- **Checklist completion not enforced**: Tasks can be marked "done" with 0% checklist items completed
- **Checklist panel fetches client-side**: Bypasses REST API/RBAC, unlike task data which goes through API routes
- **Service-role client used for site updates**: Bypasses RLS so housekeeping staff can trigger site status changes

## Next Steps
1. Fix `'housekeeping'` vs `'needs_housekeeping'` mismatch — align checkout API, HK PATCH handler, DB constraint, domain model, and sites API schema to one canonical value
2. Route site status transitions through domain model (`Site.completeHousekeeping()`) to publish `SiteStatusChangedEvent` for automation triggers
3. Add checklist completion validation before allowing task to be marked "done" (or at minimum show a warning)
4. Add checklist progress indicator to the task list table rows
5. Unify checklist data fetching to go through REST API (consistent RBAC)

## Critical Context
- **DB tables**: `checklist` (id, property_id, name, description, item JSONB, created_by, created_at, updated_at) and `housekeeping_tasks` (id, property_id, site_id, staff_id, reservation_id, checklist_id, title, description, status, priority, start_date, end_date, checklist_item_done JSON, created_by, created_at, updated_at)
- **Site status values in DB CHECK constraint**: `'available'`, `'reserved'`, `'booked'`, `'occupied'`, `'housekeeping'`, `'maintenance'`, `'unavailable'`
- **Site status values in domain model** (`src/modules/SiteManagement/domain/SiteStatus.ts`): `'available'`, `'occupied'`, `'reserved'`, `'needs_housekeeping'`, `'out_of_service'`, `'booked'` — **missing `'maintenance'` and `'unavailable'`, uses different names for 2 values**
- **Site status values in sites API Zod** (`src/types/api/v1/schemas/sites.ts`): matches domain model, not DB
- **Checkout API** (`src/app/api/v1/reservations/[id]/check-out/route.ts` line 168): writes `status: 'housekeeping'` directly to DB
- **HK PATCH handler** (`src/app/api/v1/properties/[propertyId]/housekeeping/[housekeepingId]/route.ts`): checks `normalizedStatus === 'housekeeping' || normalizedStatus === 'maintenance'` then writes `'available'` via service-role client
- **`countOpenHousekeepingTasksForSite`**: `SELECT COUNT(id) FROM housekeeping_tasks WHERE property_id=$1 AND site_id=$2 AND status != 'done'`
- **4-gate site transition**: (1) task.status==='done' → (2) openForSite===0 → (3) siteRow exists & not deleted → (4) site status is 'housekeeping' or 'maintenance'
- **Post-checkout flow**: `CheckOutDialog` → AlertDialog prompt → `AddTaskDialog` with pre-filled siteId, siteName, reservationConfirmationId
- **Checklist in tasks**: `checklistTemplateId` links to `checklist.id`; `checklistItemDone` is `Array<{item_id: string, status: 'pending'|'completed'}>` stored as JSON; `item_id` is NOT UUID-validated in Zod (accepts any string up to 120 chars)
- **Key files**: `src/lib/dashboard/housekeeping/housekeeping-queries.ts` (HousekeepingQueries class), `src/types/api/v1/schemas/housekeeping.ts` (Zod schemas), `src/components/dashboard/housekeeping/housekeeping-dialog.tsx/` (all dialogs), `src/components/dashboard/housekeeping/housekeeping-checklist/housekeeping-checklist.tsx` (checklist panel)

---

**Turn Context (split turn):**

## Original Request
The user requested a comprehensive exploration of housekeeping tasklist visibility across user roles (Owner, Admin, Manager, Staff) in Camp-OS. They wanted to understand: RBAC filtering, server-side query logic (whether staff tasks are filtered by `staff_id`), the `listHousekeepingTasks()` method's filters, how the server component passes role context to the client, how the client component uses role info for UI control, whether the assignee filter is hidden for staff, and permission checks in `resolveModuleActionAccess`.

## Early Progress
- Read three files in parallel: the housekeeping page server component, the filter component, and the API route.
- Discovered `housekeepingFallbackForCategory()` (duplicated in both page.tsx and route.ts): Owner/Admin get full CRUD, Manager gets full CRUD for housekeeping category, Staff gets **view-only** (create/update/delete all false).
- Found the filter component accepts `showAssigneeFilter?: boolean` prop (defaults `true`) — when false, the assignee dropdown is omitted and the grid layout adjusts.
- The API route's JSDoc confirms: `assigneeId` query param exists but "staff are always scoped to their own row" (elevated roles can filter by any assignee).
- The server page component calls `resolveModuleActionAccess` and `resolveUserPropertyAccess` to compute permissions before passing to client.

## Context for Suffix
- The file contents were **truncated** mid-read — the full implementations of the GET handler, page.tsx (options fetching, props assembly), and filter component (remaining filter fields) were cut off.
- **Still unread**: `src/lib/dashboard/housekeeping/housekeeping-queries.ts` (the `listHousekeepingTasks()` method and its `staffId` parameter handling) and `src/components/dashboard/housekeeping/housekeeping-page-content.tsx` (how client uses role/permissions to control UI, filter defaults, action buttons).
- The summary needs these remaining files plus the untruncated portions to fully answer the user's questions about server-side staff filtering, client-side role-based UI control, and the complete request flow.
